description:
No spec subject (candidates: specled.verification docs surface when picked up). Severity: Medium. From 2026-08-06 critical review of specled_-q0q. spec.check --run-commands executes verification commands defined in repo-resident spec files; in a CI configured to run on fork PRs this executes attacker-authored shell with the workflow token. Keep-reason: docs/policy deliverable (threat-model statement + recommended CI gating for public repos), not a code fix on the shipped branch. Concrete failure: a public repo running armed spec.check on pull_request from forks grants fork authors arbitrary command execution in CI.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: specled.package

(Orchestrator note: NOT specled.verification — that subject owns command execution
mechanics; this ticket ships no code. Model the new requirement on the existing
specled.package.adoption_guide / .concepts_guide pattern, .spec/specs/package.spec.md:104-111.)

Allowed touches:
- docs/security.md (new)
- docs/adoption.md  — the "CI should always run commands" line at docs/adoption.md:489
  must be CORRECTED, not merely supplemented. It is the unsafe advice.
- README.md
- .spec/specs/package.spec.md  (new requirement + surface: entry for docs/security.md)
- .spec/decisions/specled.decision.*.md  (only if the policy is a durable cross-cutting stance)
- CHANGELOG.md

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/** (all)
- test/** except test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs
- .spec/realization_hashes.json
- priv/spec_init/workflows/spec_review.yml.eex  (also specled.spec_review surface; widens the ticket)

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT flip the --run-commands default or add a sandbox/allowlist. This deliverable is a
  written policy. Changing the default is a separate breaking change against
  .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md.
- Do NOT name any finding code the implementation does not emit. docs/**/*.md is inside the
  doc-identifier lint corpus (test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:223) and an invented code
  name fails the gate. Show severities in bare YAML token form, not atom form
  (specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity, .spec/specs/package.spec.md:112).
- Do NOT write a generic SECURITY.md disclosure process. The ask is one threat statement
  plus the CI recommendation.

Verification:
  mix test test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs
  mix test test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format --check-formatted
  mix spec.check --no-run-commands
  bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh
No execute:false stub to flip. The doc-identifier lint is the real gate: it pins corpus size
and fails on any invented code name.

Expected diff: ~130-200 lines across 4-6 files, mostly the new doc.

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps:
- docs/security.md:11-12 understates the execution surface, in the dangerous direction, in the one sentence that enumerates it. The doc says: "`mix spec.check` executes enabled command targets by default. Several other tasks accept `--run-commands` to opt into the same behavior." Proven by execution: `mix spec.status` also executes command targets BY DEFAULT — `report_run_commands?/1` at lib/mix/tasks/spec.status.ex:77-82 is the same `{:ok, false} -> false; _ -> true` shape as spec.check, and its own moduledoc (spec.status.ex:12-14) says so outright. Only `mix spec.prime` (spec.prime.ex:87-90) and `mix spec.validate` (spec.validate.ex:69) are genuinely opt-in. So exactly two tasks execute by default; the doc names one and files the other under "opt into". This falsifies the deliverable's own subject matter: a maintainer who follows the recommended two-lane split verbatim, but whose untrusted fork lane also invokes `mix spec.status` (a maintainer-facing summary command the README lists at README.md:48 and adoption.md:239 recommends for brownfield), executes fork-authored shell with that job's token — the exact failure this ticket exists to prevent. The trap is live in the package's own scaffolding: priv/spec_init/agents/skills/spec-led-development/SKILL.md.eex:120 tells every adopting repo that `mix spec.status` is "Read-only." (that pre-existing line is out of scope to fix here, but it is why the omission is misleading rather than pedantic). Fix is one sentence: name `mix spec.status` as the second default-executing task, and restrict the "opt into" clause to `mix spec.prime` and `mix spec.validate`.

Notes (advisory only):
- docs/security.md:89-92 says `--no-run-commands` "disables `kind: command` verification targets". It also disables `kind: tagged_tests` execution, which spawns `mix test` (verifier.ex:1327-1332, tagged_tests.ex:5) and is likewise repository-controlled code. Understated in the SAFE direction (the flag disables more than advertised), but the threat section's scoping to `kind: command` leaves the second specled-owned execution kind unnamed. Same one-line class of fix.
- The GHA snippet has no `on:` trigger, so it is a fragment rather than a copy-pastable workflow; the `if:` guard on the `commands` job also evaluates false on non-`pull_request` events (`github.event.pull_request` is null), which silently disables the trusted lane on `push`. The surrounding prose does say "Adjust the setup and base-ref fetch to match your project."
- docs/adoption.md's "Wire CI" snippet still shows the armed `mix spec.check --base origin/main` form, but it is trigger-agnostic and now sits directly under the new fork-PR warning, so it does not re-assert the removed advice.
- CHANGELOG.md was in the Allowed set and was not touched. Not required by the contract; flagging in case the release note is expected at merge.
